Answer: A
Reason: The chest X-ray demonstrates complete opacification (white-out) of the left hemithorax with a distinct mediastinal shift to the right (contralateral side), which is the classic radiographic appearance of a massive pleural effusion acting as a space-occupying lesion. Tension pneumothorax would appear radiolucent (black), and lung collapse/atelectasis would cause an ipsilateral shift toward the opacity.
